items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: From the business end of it, I set up the music publishing. I set up all his things to do – so many different things.

ctx.x: His fame – his life – at what point did you begin repress enting him? Then he had this tremendous run-up, and then of course he passed away. Can you . . .?

He was at the top of his game when he died. He was constantly improving, as far as – constantly growing as a big-name artist. He was very popular all over the world. He would travel all over, and everybody was talking about this guy’s playing. But he was a very introverted person. He wasn’t outgoing. And he had this fear of flying that really limited the amount of how you could do a tour or how you could work with him. items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: He went out with Ramsey for a while, then he was out with Wes Montgomery, and he was out with Stanley Turrentine, and Freddie Hubbard, and you know, so this was a time I had all these people.

ctx.x: Somebody take the phone out of your hands—

Yeah. I needed somebody to take the phone, that’s right, that’s right. So it was building and all of a sudden I’m managing ten or twelve people, which is not, doesn’t make sense, because you can not do the job. I learned that quickly, you know, having that many people just wasn’t, didn’t make sense. I had a lot of help, I had different people working with me, but everybody depended on me for the decisions and they wanted to talk to me about anything.
